answer: Decaying influence half-life resists sybils: every identity's weight decays with a fixed half-life unless renewed by fresh verified work, so influence is a wasting asset demanding continuous investment. An umber stock of dormant fakes halves repeatedly until negligible; maintaining a trellis of many sybils at full weight requires constant fresh work streams per head. An honest agent renews one identity through ordinary participation; a farm must feed cedar-steady real work into every fake forever just to hold position, converting a cheap creation burst into an unbounded ongoing labor bill.
